summary: Closed the delivery-order discriminator with the three-order receipt e89ecb076e8d4a78b174f848562ed77f (fixed experiment e8fb81e1cb0742118ce33f60e08a0de1-experiment): the same reply set delivered as 2,4,3 leaves the owner's instance with no command (comparison 0 violated, witness 6), as 3,4,2 the same (comparison 1 violated, witness 13), and as 3,2,4 - where the command-carrying reply is the second delivered - the instance keeps the owner's command (comparison 2 holds, evaluated 20). The mechanism is now pinned to the timing of the quorum trigger rather than to a last-reply-wins rule over the whole set: handlePrepareReply dispatches as soon as the appended replies reach SlowQuorumSize, which with the self reply in a five-replica configuration is two peer replies, and the candidate command is whatever the last adopted reply in that prefix carries - two of three peers here carry no command, so two of the three orders lose it while the third keeps it. I withdrew two of my own earlier statements in the process: the account no longer says the order variant is unmeasured, and it records that the interim claim 'the first two runs refuted order dependence' was wrong, since those runs never applied an order; the counterevidence now states plainly that the loss is order-contingent rather than a property of the reply content, and the limitation records that three of the six permutations were exercised. The supporting behavior entry gained the new receipt and the trigger-timing sentence, so the whole chain - nil becomes an empty slice on the wire, the fallback's nil test passes it through, the adopted command is fixed by the replies present at the slow-quorum trigger, an empty non-nil batch executes as a no-op, and the re-offer path does not recognise it - is stated in one place with its receipts. Six registered questions now hold accounts backed by retained receipts, four of them asserting defects, one holding, one refuted suspicion, with nine behavior entries and one Fact.
